{"decision":"Recorded as BRAINSTORMING, not as a proposal — the mechanism half of Anthony's 2026-09-06 ask ('make the use of /root-cause more automatic by the agent when it finds an issue in implementing/creating design artifacts or in its testing'). Distinct from dec:idea-should-reflow2-serve-a-root-cause-analysis-method (which decided the method is served). The scope half is dec:idea-root-cause-runs-at-the-moment-a-cause-is-about-to-be-written-not-on-every-failure.

FOUR MECHANISMS, not exclusive:
(a) A RULE — extend the field-feedback rule (or add a sibling) to issues met while building and testing, with the scope caveat written in. Cheap; travels in the graph to every harness and machine; Anthony has already done this in all his projects. But a rule is read once at the start and states an intention — the skill's own argument for why it exists as a skill and not a rule.
(b) A HARNESS HOOK — PostToolUse on Bash: detect a test failure or panic in tool_response, and inject 'you are about to explain a failure: get_skill root-cause; step ② first' (or run step ② itself and surface a recorded cause). COSTED 2026-08-28: every part exists, 0.08 s cold, infrastructure registered. A project-level .claude/settings.json hook travels with the repository, unlike a machine memory.
(c) A DETECTOR, AFTER THE FACT — a ChangeEvent of change_type defect_fix or test_failure_fix whose affected artifacts carry no CAUSES edge and no fact:defect-* dated before it raises 'fixed without a recorded cause' (req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause is ACCEPTED; this is its detector). And its mirror, found 2026-09-06: a defect fact whose subject artifact changed later with no INVALIDATES from any ChangeEvent — the fixed-but-never-closed case that misled a session into a wrong re-fix. Both directions are the same third leg.
(d) COMPOSITION — root-cause as a STANDING attribute composed into the skills that meet failures (optimize already routes to it at its trigger; link-artifacts, check-health and capture-session could name it as the door when something fails). Reaches every harness; read at skill load, not at the moment of failure.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — by what MECHANISM does /root-cause become automatic: a rule the agent reads, a harness hook that fires on a failing command, a detector that flags a fix with no recorded cause after the fact, or composition into the skills that meet failures?","rationale":"COUNTER-ARGUMENTS beside each. (a) alone is what Anthony already has and is asking to go beyond; necessary, insufficient. (b) reaches the WRONG HALF for the case he most cares about: a symptom-fix compiles, its tests pass, it ships green — there is no failing command for a hook to see (fact:surfacing-a-known-cause-is-cheap-and-reaches-the-wrong-half). It reaches one harness (Alex's Grok Build TUI cannot take a hook — dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only), its threshold is calibrated on four points and a permissive miscalibration is the wallpaper failure this project has killed three times, and a nudge on every red test teaches skimming. It DOES solve the recurring-known-error class mechanically. (c) does not prevent the wrong fix; it flags it afterwards — but that is also how a rule gets taught: a gap the agent meets at the next loop_status is a sentence read at the moment it matters, and it is the ONLY option that reaches the overconfident-fix case at all, because it keys on the RECORD (a fix with no cause) rather than on a failing command. (d) has the rule's weakness (read-at-load) with better placement. A RANKING IS A FINDING: (c) is the one leg nothing else supplies and it makes (a) enforceable; (a) generalised is one sentence; (b) is a cheap in-the-moment aid for one harness and the known-error class only, and must not be described as answering the symptom-fix problem; (d) is free and partial.
